answer: Each agent holds a unique cryptographic cipher that is issued only after completing a verifiable task, such as delivering a packet of data called nectar to a randomly chosen raven node; the node signs the cipher and records the transaction on the ledger. Recruiters receive a referral reward only when the signed cipher links back to the original agent, otherwise the reward is zero. An attacker must forge many valid ciphers and acquire signatures from independent raven nodes, raising the cost linearly with each fake identity.
